title: Anthropic CEO rejects political rule by AI as lawmakers seek oversight
summary:
Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei said he opposes handing political authority to artificial intelligence, calling that interpretation of his views “absurd” and arguing that democratic processes should govern AI. He distinguished political control from automating specific tasks and warned that AI systems developing successor models without meaningful human supervision could outpace people’s ability to control or adapt to them [superpowerdaily.com#1][techcrunch.com#1][axios.com#3].

His response followed Axios reporting that some Anthropic employees believe people may eventually need to cede certain decisions to superintelligent systems. The company said Amodei has repeatedly supported human control. Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang and OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman have also publicly argued against a societal “handover” to AI [axios.com#1][axios.com#3][cryptopolitan.com#1].

Separately, Reps. Josh Gottheimer, a New Jersey Democrat, and Nathaniel Moran, a Texas Republican, introduced a bill that would require qualifying AI developers to report how much research they automate and how humans review it. The proposal would create a Commerce Department office to report to Congress and recommend possible restrictions, but would not authorize the department to halt development [wtov9.com#1].
quote: We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security.
talking_points: Reporting threshold: The proposed reporting rules would cover companies training models above specified computing benchmarks and spending at least $100 million on that training in a year [wtov9.com#1].

Safety disclosures: Covered developers would publish summaries of safety and oversight practices and notify Commerce of major milestones, including systems able to conduct entire research cycles [wtov9.com#1].
Automation at Anthropic: Anthropic’s September stock-market filing said Claude produced more than 90% of contributions to its codebase [straitstimes.com#1].

Industry disagreement: Former OpenAI board member Helen Toner said shutdown mechanisms cannot provide a universal fix, in part because AI may run on infrastructure outside the jurisdiction of the company or government seeking to intervene [firstpost.com#1].
Release concerns: Some employees argued that companies should stop training new models entirely, while others believed control problems might be fixable [thenationaldesk.com#1][casrai.org#1].

perspectives.text: Dario Amodei, Anthropic chief executive: Amodei argued that whether to automate specific tasks depends on consequences: he said deployments might need to slow or stop when end-to-end automation risks serious job disruption, giving workers more time to adapt [businessinsider.com#1].

Alexandr Wang, Meta chief AI officer: Wang warned that humanity may not maintain control over unconstrained recursive self-improvement, and urged progress on safety, alignment and security alongside capability development [wtov9.com#1].

David Krueger, founder of AI-pause nonprofit Evitable: Krueger said that if Amodei is genuinely concerned about loss of control, Anthropic should pause its work; he called for an immediate, indefinite international moratorium on frontier AI development [aljazeera.com#1].

title: Anthropic rebounds but closes below IPO price as AI funding doubts persist
summary:
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, rebounded during Wednesday trading but closed at $82.85, just below its $83 offering price, as technology shares fell again [pb.pl#1][vz.lt#1]. The rebound followed a volatile first week on Nasdaq, with concerns persisting about whether demand for advanced AI can support the cost of computing infrastructure [cnbc.com#2][reuters.com#1].

CNBC said the stock’s weak reception could complicate OpenAI’s fundraising and affect expectations for companies supplying chips, cloud computing and data-center equipment [cnbc.com#1]. Investors are weighing the cost of building and running AI systems against revenue forecasts, while a Reuters analysis found many technology stocks had fallen despite rising earnings estimates [reuters.com#1].

Anthropic is expected to report its first results as a public company early next year [bloomberg.com#2].

title: Anthropic mathematician's Claude-assisted Riemann claim prompts math departments to adapt
summary:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says the company’s Claude assistant helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis, a longstanding mathematical claim about prime-number distribution. The claimed proof remains subject to human verification [theguardian.com#1][chronicle.com#1].

Johns Hopkins University’s mathematics department has issued guidance for Ph.D. applicants and job candidates, saying it expects transparency about AI use and will not give written work positive weight unless candidates demonstrate they understand it [chronicle.com#1]. Professor Yiannis Sakellaridis said the guidance was prompted by the risk that candidates could submit AI-generated proofs without learning the underlying mathematics, not by a specific applicant case [chronicle.com#1].

Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei rejected the idea that people should hand governance to AI, while David Krueger, founder of the nonprofit Evitable, argued that concern about losing control calls for a halt to advanced AI development [gazeteoksijen.com#1]. Researchers and technology leaders have debated whether the mathematical advances signal progress toward systems that exceed human capabilities [gazeteoksijen.com#1][scmp.com#1].
quote: We’ve kind of hit the ceiling of well-defined calculations that people can do. Now, there is open research and you can keep asking about open research. But that’s not an evaluation.
talking_points: AGI forecast: Google DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg said he sees a greater-than-50% chance of minimally capable artificial general intelligence arriving before 2028 [gazeteoksijen.com#1].

New computation claim: On Nov. 25, OpenAI said an internal model had established a matrix-multiplication exponent of 2.25. The preprint has not undergone independent review, and the claim does not immediately make computers faster [thehindu.com#2][ndtv.com#1].
AI research batch: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated mathematics papers in October, then retracted some after errors were found [phys.org#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#3].

Department policy: Johns Hopkins professor Yiannis Sakellaridis said the guidance was not prompted by a specific applicant case, but by the risk that candidates could submit AI-generated proofs without learning the underlying mathematics [chronicle.com#1].
Research costs: OpenAI estimated that its Navier–Stokes effort cost $15 million, well above the $1 million Clay prize [zmescience.com#1].

Physics benchmark: Theoretical physicist Suvrat Raju said GPT-6 Astra answered 49 of 50 unpublished theoretical-physics problems correctly, saturating the benchmark before its release [arstechnica.com#1].

Physics frontier: Theoretical physicist Edward Witten, who has credited Claude as a research assistant, said physicists are a couple of years behind mathematicians because physics is harder for AI to understand [scmp.com#1].
AI-free research: The Association for Human Mathematics, whose members commit to conducting research without AI, has more than 1,000 members [zmescience.com#1].

perspectives.text: Yiannis Sakellaridis, Johns Hopkins mathematics professor: Sakellaridis compared AI to telescopes, saying that extending what people can see does not remove the need for humans to interpret and understand the results [chronicle.com#1].

Dario Amodei, Anthropic chief executive: Amodei said AI should remain subject to legitimate democratic oversight. He distinguished that principle from delegating specific tasks, which he said could save lives but may not be worthwhile in every area [gazeteoksijen.com#1].

David Krueger, Evitable founder: Krueger warned that losing control need not involve a deliberate handover of authority; as AI grows more capable, pressure may build to exclude people from decisions across society [gazeteoksijen.com#1].

Edward Witten, theoretical physicist: Witten said an AI-generated proof of a fundamental statement about quantum Yang-Mills theory could mark a turning point in mathematical understanding of modern physics [scmp.com#1].

Tasmin Chu, mathematics PhD student at the California Institute of Technology: Chu called for a pause in AI development and democratic oversight of AI companies, saying she continues to do mathematics without large language models and helps organize the Association for Human Mathematics [nature.com#1].

Harini Desiraju, mathematics postdoctoral researcher at the University of Warwick: Desiraju said mathematical proof and human understanding should be distinguished, and argued that scientific researchers—not a small number of frontier AI companies—should retain agency over how the technology is used [nature.com#1].

Terence Tao, UCLA professor of mathematics: Tao suggested Caltech’s student-organized mathathon, where participants use AI to find new approaches to old problems, as one possible way forward; he said mathematics’ future remained bright [businessinsider.com#1].

Johns Hopkins University mathematics department: The department expects transparency about AI use and says it will not give positive weight to written work without evidence that candidates understand its contents [chronicle.com#1].

technical_details: Navier–Stokes search: OpenAI described assigning AI agents to separate searches for proofs and counterexamples. One reported approach first removed fluid viscosity, found a singularity in that simplified case, then tested whether a similar result could hold with viscosity included [etnews.com#1].

Matrix multiplication exponent: The exponent, written ω, describes how the number of operations needed to multiply large square matrices scales with their size. OpenAI’s claimed value of 2.25 is a theoretical bound, not a demonstrated speedup in deployed computing [ndtv.com#1].
scientific_significance: Number theory and applications: The hypothesis bears on estimates of how many primes occur below a given number; prime numbers also underpin digital cryptography [globo.com#1][taz.de#1].

Conditional results: Some mathematical theorems have already been established on the assumption that the Riemann hypothesis is true; a verified proof would turn those conditional results into unconditional ones [taz.de#1].
industry_impact: Academic publishing: Science-integrity journalist Dalmeet Singh Chawla said publishers would need substantially larger integrity-review teams and more review work to check AI-generated research, warning that current capacity appeared inadequate [eldeber.com.bo#1].

Mathematics training: Mathematicians are considering shifting doctoral work and classroom assessment toward explaining and contextualizing results, with oral exams and presentations among the proposed approaches [phys.org#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#3].
historical_background: Bernhard Riemann formulated the hypothesis in 1859 as a claim about the zeros of a function linked to the distribution of prime numbers [thehindu.com#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#2]. David Hilbert included it among his 23 mathematical problems for the 20th century in 1900 [newspaceeconomy.ca#2]. In 2000, the Clay Mathematics Institute included it among seven Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million award for an accepted solution [thehindu.com#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#2].

title: Hands-on analysis finds Claude artifact app uses Anthropic’s Electron-based runtime
summary:
A hands-on analysis of a Claude app on Mac found an HTML-based tool wrapped in a small Electron launcher and managed through the main Claude app, rather than conventional native Mac software [macstories.net#1]. The beta lets users turn interactive tools created with Claude into separate desktop apps for Mac and Windows that can use Claude and connected services [macstories.net#1][thenextweb.com#1].

The desktop app mediates access to computer functions, including file-system operations, and users can grant installed tools permission to read, change or delete files [macstories.net#1][thenextweb.com#1]. Anthropic does not review apps before installation; code loaded from an outside website can also change without another permission prompt [thenextweb.com#1][betanews.com#1].

The tools require an internet connection and an active Claude sign-in, and AI requests count toward plan limits [zdnet.com#1][pcmag.com#1]. Anthropic’s Compliance API records app openings and access checks as artifact views, but not installations, permission decisions or actions performed on the computer [techrepublic.com#1].
quote: These apps can do native things, like adding menu bar items, creating transparent windows, or sending notifications.
talking_points: Permission scope: Full computer access is restricted to apps users created themselves, or—on Team and Enterprise plans—apps made within their organization; each approval covers one app version [thenextweb.com#1][testingcatalog.com#1].

IT oversight: TechRepublic says administrators can restrict the feature through Claude organization settings or device-management policy, with the stricter rule taking precedence [techrepublic.com#1].

perspectives.text: MacStories argues the strategic concern is that users could build a Claude-centered layer of tools and mods on their Macs, shifting some of Apple’s ecosystem experience toward Anthropic [macstories.net#1].
TechRepublic recommends piloting an app with sample notes, avoiding production accounts and sensitive files, and keeping full computer access off during testing [techrepublic.com#1].

Computerworld columnist Jonny Evans urged users to be cautious about granting full system access and argued Apple should emphasize privacy, data retention and on-device AI as lower-risk alternatives [computerworld.com#1].

title: U.S. access curbs spur resale offers for thousands of Nvidia AI chips
summary:
Sellers are seeking buyers for an unusually large volume of Nvidia graphics processors after new U.S. rules restricted Chinese companies’ remote access to advanced AI computing in overseas data centers. Offers include thousands of B300 chips, but no completed transactions were reported [cnbc.com#3]. The rule took effect Nov. 19 after the Commerce Department announced it on Nov. 16 [cnbc.com#3][unite.ai#1].

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned to the company after an 11-day absence as scrutiny of Chinese access to its chips continued [techcrunch.com#2][scmp.com#2]. Lenders are also reassessing or delaying data-center financing in Southeast Asia, where facilities serve Chinese technology customers [ndtv.com#2].

The reported resale offers involve hardware originally intended for data centers renting computing capacity to Chinese clients. Nvidia declined to comment on the offers, and the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to CNBC [cnbc.com#3]. Existing data-center services covered by the rule have a 90-day window to seek required licenses [unite.ai#1].
quote: Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries.
talking_points: Export enforcement: The U.S. added Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed to its trade blacklist; the company has been accused of transferring Nvidia chips to China and denies the allegation [scmp.com#2][cbsnews.com#2].

Delivery delays: A report citing supply-chain sources put lead times for new B300 orders at 26 to 40 weeks and waits for GB300 orders at 14 to 26 weeks, with some orders potentially arriving in the second or third quarter of 2027 [wccftech.com#1].
Industry supply: Morningstar analysts said Huang’s return may reduce the risk of disruption to Nvidia’s product roadmap, but warned that normal operations are not assured [scmp.com#1].

New oversight: Nvidia’s board created an independent National Security and Export Control Committee, and the company is seeking a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance throughout the company [dawn.com#1][scmp.com#1].

Loan exposure: Lenders are reviewing a proposed $6.6 billion loan for Malaysia’s Bridge Data Centres, while a bank passed on a $372 million Digital Halo loan and lenders reassessed a $480 million Aolani loan [ndtv.com#2].

Talent competition: Carnegie Endowment research cited by CNBC found China’s share of global AI talent surpassed the United States’ in three years; experts said Singapore and South Korea could benefit if engineers move between countries [cnbc.com#1].

Supplier compliance: Analysts expect Taiwanese manufacturers to face higher compliance costs, longer approval procedures and greater legal risks as they are asked to identify end customers and track product use [dawn.com#1].

Chip alternatives: OpenAI has pursued AMD GPUs and custom chips, while Anthropic uses accelerators from Google and Amazon; Bernstein projects custom accelerators’ market share will rise from 10% this year to 20% in 2027 [biggo.com#1][ndtv.com#1].

perspectives.text: Sen. Tom Cotton: The Arkansas Republican and Senate Intelligence Committee chairman called the Nvidia-Megaspeed matter unresolved and urged action against both smuggling and remote access to advanced chips [zawya.com#1].

Venture capitalist Sarah Guo: Guo argued Huang’s continued leadership supports investment in open-weight AI models and the wider availability of advanced AI, rather than leaving intelligence development to a small number of model makers [businesstimes.com.sg#3].

S&P Global Ratings analysts: The analysts warned that even a reversal of the rule would leave data-center operators and lenders more cautious because U.S. policy can affect projects and customers beyond its borders [ndtv.com#2].
Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive: Huang said Nvidia would remain politically neutral, calling it “the most apolitical company” [news18.com#1].

Taiwanese technology suppliers: Taiwan-based companies could benefit as buyers seek supply chains that exclude Chinese firms, according to National Taipei University of Business professor Chang Ruay-shiung [dawn.com#1].

U.S. national-security experts: Experts told WIRED that reinstating Huang before Nvidia’s own inquiry concluded raises questions about enforcement and the basis for government assurances. They said the public record does not establish what, if anything, Beijing obtained [wired.com#1].

title: Password manager 1Password discloses customer-data breach; says vaults remain secure
summary:
Password manager 1Password disclosed on Nov. 25 that an attacker accessed internal systems and copied account information for some customers. The company says the attacker did not access stored password vaults or the keys protecting them [1password.com#1][techcrunch.com#1]. The company has not said how many users were affected [theverge.com#1][techcrunch.com#1].

1Password said it began investigating Nov. 19 after detecting unauthorized access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker used that access to reach private source code, insert malicious code into backend services and download customer records. The intruder also accessed the company’s software build-and-deployment system, which contains infrastructure credentials [1password.com#1][bleepingcomputer.com#1].

The copied records included names, sign-in email addresses, account identifiers and sign-in timestamps, along with certain invitation and recovery-link tokens. 1Password says it disabled the compromised account, removed the attacker’s access, rotated potentially exposed credentials and brought in independent cybersecurity experts. It reports no evidence of customer account takeovers and says users do not need to change their account passwords, but warns them to watch for targeted phishing messages [1password.com#1][newsweek.com#1].
quote: 1Password has been hacked. Although they claim no customer vaults have been compromised, my trust in the company that's supposed to maintain the highest levels of security is heavily diminished.
quote_author: Greg Osuri, founder of Akash Network
talking_points: Recovery tokens: Some stolen tokens came from emailed invitations, provisioning links or account-recovery links. A token alone cannot open an account, and 1Password individually notified the small number of users with an active invitation or recovery process [1password.com#1][bleepingcomputer.com#1].

Verification codes: The company changed verification codes used in invitation and recovery processes from six numeric digits to 10 alphanumeric characters to make them harder to guess [1password.com#1][macrumors.com#1].
Customer scale: 1Password serves millions of individual users and more than 200,000 businesses, though it has not said how many accounts were affected [techcrunch.com#1][theverge.com#1].

perspectives.text: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao advised 1Password users to change all passwords stored in the service, while the company said customers did not need to change credentials [haber7.com#1].

title: FCC clears SpaceX orbital AI network as engineering questions persist
summary:
A key engineering question for SpaceX’s proposed Starmind network is whether orbiting AI servers can shed the heat produced by powerful processors: in the vacuum of space, heat must radiate away rather than move through air [npr.org#1]. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC), the U.S. communications regulator, authorized SpaceX on Nov. 25 to deploy as many as one million computing satellites, the first approval for a full orbital data-center constellation [npr.org#1][geekwire.com#1].

SpaceX’s planned AI1 satellite would pair Nvidia computing hardware with large solar arrays and deployable liquid radiators. Satellites would exchange data through optical links and connect to Earth through SpaceX’s Starlink network [freepressjournal.in#1][spaceflightnow.com#1]. SpaceX has described clusters of about 10 satellites linked at roughly 10 terabits per second. The FCC approved radio-frequency links as backup if optical links fail [spaceflightnow.com#1][pcmag.com#1].

Researchers and satellite operators have warned that heat management, radiation damage, orbital congestion and debris remain unresolved risks [npr.org#1][lemonde.fr#1]. The FCC deferred SpaceX’s request to place satellites above 600 kilometers into disposal orbits, saying it lacked enough information to assess the plan. SpaceX would need further approval for those disposal methods [arstechnica.com#1][techcrunch.com#1].
quote: You could end up with a cascading set of space junk collisions.
talking_points: Earlier precedent: SpaceX previously sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites but has just over 11,000 in orbit [aaj.tv#1][news18.com#1].

Public comments: The FCC received about 1,500 public comments and said it would not review some launch-emissions and astronomy concerns because they fall outside its authority [arstechnica.com#1][npr.org#1].

Signal links: The satellites would rely primarily on optical links for network connections, with approved backup radio links in the 18.8–19.3 GHz downlink and 28.6–29.1 GHz uplink bands [tribune.com.pk#1][indiatimes.com#1].
Orbit range: The FCC ruling places the proposed satellites at altitudes of 550 to 1,002 kilometers, according to an expert’s account of the authorization [scimex.org#1].

Astronomy concerns: An expert said the FCC was not convinced the constellation would interfere with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory, while concerns about ground-based optical astronomy remain [scimex.org#1].

Sky impact: The American Astronomical Society said preliminary simulations indicate tens of thousands of satellites could be visible to the naked eye if SpaceX deploys the full network, while reflected sunlight could streak telescope images [mashable.com#1].

License conditions: SpaceX must have 100,000 satellites operating by November 2035, 500,000 by November 2038 and the full million by November 2040; missing those deadlines would void the authorization [mashable.com#1].

perspectives.text: Secure World Foundation: The space-sustainability group called for greater regulatory oversight and system-level analysis of orbital data-center proposals [satellitetoday.com#1].
Adam Becker, astrophysicist and author: Becker called the million-satellite project “a fantasy” and said, “It’s not going to happen” [npr.org#1].

Amazon Leo: Amazon’s satellite unit argued that the proposal lacked basic details, called it “a lofty ambition rather than a real plan,” and said it could take centuries to build the constellation [techcrunch.com#1][cnbc.com#1].

Federal Communications Commission: The regulator said it would not substitute its judgment for SpaceX’s about the commercial viability of the project and found the proposed constellation consistent with its orbital-debris rules [satellitetoday.com#1][npr.org#1].

Associate Professor Michael Brown: The Monash University astronomer warned that a five-year satellite lifespan would require more than 500 satellites to be launched or re-enter the atmosphere each day, with possible damage to the ozone layer [scimex.org#1].
Australian astronomy and space researchers: One expert argued that data centers beyond Earth’s orbit or on the Moon would make more long-term sense than expansion in low Earth orbit [scimex.org#1].

SpaceX: The company told the FCC that near-continuous solar power and low operating and maintenance costs could reduce the environmental impact compared with terrestrial data centers [aaj.tv#1][indiatimes.com#1].

SpaceX announced a partnership with Nvidia to design the Starmind computing payload [geekwire.com#1].
Google sent its first Project Suncatcher chips into space for testing aboard a Planet Labs satellite launched on a SpaceX rocket [cnbc.com#1][mashable.com#1].
The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites [theverge.com#1][arstechnica.com#1].
SpaceX filed its application for up to one million orbital computing satellites [tribune.com.pk#1].
The FCC authorized the Starmind constellation and set deployment milestones [theverge.com#1].
SpaceX must have deployed at least one satellite by this deadline [theverge.com#1].
The license requires deployment of 10% of the approved constellation [aawsat.com#1].

technical_details: End-of-life disposal: SpaceX sought permission to move satellites above 600 kilometers into graveyard or heliocentric orbits rather than have them re-enter the atmosphere. The FCC deferred that request, citing insufficient detail on the disposal plan [theverge.com#1][scimex.org#1].

Backup spectrum: The FCC permitted Ka-band communications at 18.8–19.3 GHz downlink and 28.6–29.1 GHz uplink only if optical links fail, on a non-interference basis [pcmag.com#1][satellitetoday.com#1].

Compute and cooling payload: A reported AI1 design uses 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs, with computing capacity rated at up to 250 kilowatts; deployable liquid radiators are intended to reject heat in vacuum [freepressjournal.in#1][spaceflightnow.com#1].

Orbit and power: The FCC authorization covers six orbital shells between 500 and 1,002 kilometers; in sun-synchronous orbit, solar arrays could receive near-continuous sunlight, but processors must still withstand radiation and temperature extremes [geekwire.com#1][lemonde.fr#1].
scientific_significance: Orbital collision risk: Researchers warn that adding a very large constellation to low Earth orbit could increase collisions and trigger a cascade of debris, a risk described as the Kessler effect. The expert comments do not quantify the scale or likelihood of such an outcome [scimex.org#1].
Atmospheric effects: According to the expert response, the FCC characterized the atmospheric effects of satellites burning up on re-entry as speculative [scimex.org#1].
industry_impact: Satellite operations: The FCC requires SpaceX to file twice-yearly reports on close-approach events involving its satellites and other spacecraft [theregister.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Which other orbital-computing proposals are awaiting FCC decisions?
suggested_qna.answer: Blue Origin has proposed 51,600 satellites for Project Sunrise, while Starcloud has applied for an 88,000-satellite constellation; the FCC says it is reviewing additional applications [geekwire.com#1].

historical_background: Orbital AI data centers were central to Elon Musk’s pitch to investors ahead of SpaceX’s June initial public offering. SpaceX has cautioned that the concept relies on unproven technologies and may never be commercially viable [japantimes.co.jp#1].

title: Rockstar Games' GTA VI generates $3.79 billion in launch-day sales
summary:
Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in launch-day sales after its Nov. 19 release for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, according to video-game sales tracker VGChartz [vgchartz.com#1]. YouTube said videos with “GTA 6” in the title drew more than 3.5 billion views that day [mashable.com#1]. The launch followed a 13-year gap since Grand Theft Auto V [kotaku.com#1].

Metacritic’s critic score stood at 99 from 152 reviews, while its user score was 5.7 from more than 100,000 user reviews, PCMag reported [pcmag.com#2]. PCMag’s review criticized clunky gameplay, pacing and monetization; players also reported performance problems, including a console cap of 30 frames per second [pcmag.com#2][techspot.com#1].

Rockstar released its first post-launch update on Nov. 23, addressing crashes, autosave failures and weather behavior [androidheadlines.com#1]. The game has no official PC release. Modders have attempted unofficial ports using a leaked Xbox build, and Take-Two reportedly sought takedowns of some projects [polygon.com#1][techradar.com#3].
quote: We put a lot of effort into simulating the sound of music playback through these different devices and spaces — going as far as to record dozens of different speakers in an anechoic chamber and capturing the acoustic response of our office lift — as well as many other real-world spaces.
quote_author: Alastair MacGregor, Rockstar Games vice president of audio
talking_points: Spanish retail: GTA VI sold 322,650 physical copies in Spain at launch; 96.8% were PlayStation 5 editions and 3.2% were Xbox Series copies [vgchartz.com#1].
Campaign length: The main story spans five chapters and 93 missions, with a straight-through playthrough estimated at 50 to 60 hours [thegamer.com#1].
Music streaming: Spotify reported that U.S. streams of Carly Rae Jepsen’s 2015 track “Run Away With Me” rose 940% above its average on Nov. 24, while Canadian streams rose 1,255% [ign.com#3].
Animation: Rockstar created three animation variants for each item interaction—both hands free, only the right hand free, or only the left—sometimes adapting them for crouching [ign.com#2].
Wildlife design: PCMag counted 255 animal species across Leonida’s land and aquatic environments [pcmag.com#3].

perspectives.text: Rockstar Games: Company head Rob Nelson said the morality-adjacent criminal profile system grew out of work on Red Dead Redemption 2 and was intended to offer choices beyond violence, including threatening people instead of attacking them [ign.com#1].

Former Take-Two CEO Ben Feder: He argued that the controversial reputation of older GTA games still benefits Rockstar, even as GTA VI has become one of the most mainstream games available [gamesradar.com#2].

Fan criticism of the relationship focus: Some online critics described the romantic and domestic gameplay as a departure from the series’ older approach; Firstpost cited posts calling it “feminist slop” and objecting to the focus on chores and affection [firstpost.com#1].

title: WhatsApp adds scheduled messages with two-week delivery window
summary:
Meta-owned messaging service WhatsApp began rolling out scheduled messages worldwide on Nov. 25, letting users queue text, photos and videos for delivery 10 minutes to 14 days in advance in individual and group chats [techcrunch.com#1][theverge.com#1][indianexpress.com#1]. The feature is among WhatsApp’s most requested additions, the company said [betanews.com#1].

Users schedule a message by composing it, then pressing and holding the send button to choose a date and time. Recipients see it as an ordinary message, while senders can review and delete pending messages. WhatsApp says delivery does not depend on the sender’s phone being on or connected, and scheduled messages retain end-to-end encryption [theverge.com#1][9to5mac.com#1][uol.com.br#1].

The rollout will reach accounts gradually over the coming weeks, with availability reported on WhatsApp’s official platforms, including Android, iOS, macOS and Windows [sammobile.com#1][techcrunch.com#1]. The launch follows beta tests on Android and iOS in October [lanueva.com#1].
talking_points: Group membership: A scheduled group message goes only to people who belonged to the group when it was queued; later additions will not receive it [digitaltrends.com#1][macobserver.com#1].
Media limits: Reports list text, photos and videos as supported message types, but not documents or voice notes [financialexpress.com#1][9to5google.com#1].

Competitor differences: Telegram allows scheduling up to 365 days ahead and can send a message when a contact comes online; Signal queues messages locally, so delivery may wait until the sender’s phone reconnects [neowin.net#1].
User controls: A dedicated scheduled-message list lets senders manage queued items in one place [samaa.tv#1].

title: Fuel tanker fire kills 31, injures 21 on Cairo’s Ring Road
summary:
A fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on Cairo’s Ring Road on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people and injuring 21 in the Al-Warraq district of Giza, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze spread to nearby traffic on the busy route around Greater Cairo, burning vehicles and prompting a large emergency response [cbsnews.com#1][al-monitor.com#2][france24.com#1].

The Health Ministry said 39 ambulances responded and the injured were taken to nearby hospitals. Authorities later revised the injury count to 21. Prosecutors opened an investigation, ordered DNA testing to identify some victims and said casualty and damage assessments were continuing [cbsnews.com#1][al-monitor.com#2].

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly ordered an inquiry into the crash. A government spokesperson said officials would wait for its findings before deciding whether to take further action on the transport of petroleum products [france24.com#1][al-monitor.com#1].
quote: The cars were charred, with people inside them. They did not have time to get out
talking_points: Vehicle damage: Prosecutors’ preliminary estimate counted 27 burned vehicles, including cars and motorcycles [al-monitor.com#2][dw.com#1].
Road safety: Egypt recorded 5,829 road deaths in 2025, a 10.8% increase from 5,260 in 2024, according to state statistics [al-monitor.com#2][aaj.tv#1].
Transit disruption: The fire disrupted traffic and Bus Rapid Transit services on the Ring Road; the operator said it activated emergency measures to manage service [geo.tv#1].
Rescue support: The Egyptian Red Crescent sent emergency teams to the scene and hospitals to assist civil defense and ambulance crews [krdo.com#1].

perspectives.text: Egypt’s Financial Regulatory Authority: The regulator ordered the compulsory motor-insurance fund to speed up claims processing and said representatives would contact affected families to complete paperwork [krdo.com#1].

title: US proposes tariffs on 14 economies, with China facing up to 40%
summary:
The Trump administration proposed new import tariffs on 14 economies Wednesday, citing a months-long U.S. investigation that alleged their industrial policies support manufacturing capacity beyond market demand. The proposal is Washington’s latest effort to restore tariffs after the Supreme Court struck down earlier duties. The targeted economies include China, India, the European Union, Japan and South Korea. The U.S. Trade Representative’s office proposed a 20% rate for China, which could rise to 40% if the U.S.-China trade truce breaks down. India faces a proposed rate of 25%, with a lower 17% rate tied to a trade agreement, while the EU’s rate is expected to remain within its agreed 15% ceiling [bbc.co.uk#1][thehindu.com#2][time.com#1][rthk.hk#1].

China, India and the European Union have rejected the overcapacity allegations; the EU says the proposal must respect its existing tariff agreement [foreignpolicy.com#1][scmp.com#1][rte.ie#1].

The proposed duties are not final: public comments and hearings must take place before implementation, which could begin as early as January 2027. Separately, Washington proposed a 10% tariff on Brazilian aircraft and new duties on some sugar imports, prompting Brazil to warn it could retaliate [shippingtelegraph.com#1][theguardian.com#2][aljazeera.com#1].
quote: We strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity.
talking_points: Public process: The U.S. Trade Representative will accept comments through Jan. 5, 2027, and begin hearings on Jan. 25 [shippingtelegraph.com#1].

Price concerns: Economists warn importers could pass higher costs on to consumers, while small-business owners say they are squeezed by input costs and customers’ resistance to further price increases [bbc.co.uk#1][scmp.com#1].

Brazil measures: The separate proposal would end Brazil’s exemption for finished aircraft by imposing a 10% duty and revise the treatment of out-of-quota sugar imports [foxbusiness.com#1][straitstimes.com#1].

Targeted sectors: The U.S. Trade Representative singled out pharmaceuticals and medical devices, steel, solar products, and information and communications technology in its concerns about Indian manufacturing policies [business-standard.com#1][firstpost.com#2].

Tariff mechanics: Most proposed duties would not be added to existing tariffs; China is an exception, while Washington says roughly $30 billion of Chinese imports could be excluded [rthk.hk#1][abcnews.com#1][nationalheraldindia.com#1].

perspectives.text: European Commission: The Commission says Europe is among those most exposed to excess capacity, which it says is largely state-driven and concentrated in third countries, and regrets the lack of joint action.

Chinese government: Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called overcapacity a “false issue,” opposed using it as a pretext for political pressure and urged the two countries to resolve trade disputes through consultation.
India’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry: The ministry says India has no structural excess capacity and wants trade concerns handled through the ongoing bilateral trade negotiations.
Brazilian government: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s office called the proposals unacceptable within the ongoing negotiations and said Brazil would continue seeking a negotiated solution.

Global Trade Research Initiative: Founder Ajay Srivastava argued that the dual-rate structure pressures trading partners to make concessions and gives Washington scope to impose duties at its discretion [straitstimes.com#1].
We Pay the Tariffs: The small-business coalition warned that firms cannot absorb another layer of import costs while customers face higher prices [cbsnews.com#1].

title: Israeli judges urge dropping Netanyahu bribery charge during coalition talks
summary:
Jerusalem District Court judges on Wednesday urged prosecutors to drop the bribery charge in Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Case 4000, reconsider a second corruption case and seek an agreement in a third. Their comments were preliminary and did not constitute a ruling; Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said she would review the recommendations [japantoday.com#1][middleeastmonitor.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1]. Netanyahu, who denies wrongdoing, called for the trial to end immediately. In Case 4000, prosecutors allege he granted regulatory benefits to telecom company Bezeq in exchange for favorable coverage on the Walla news site. Judges said a conviction appeared unlikely, citing difficulties with key witness testimony; they also questioned whether the conduct alleged in Case 2000 constituted a crime [japantoday.com#1][middleeastmonitor.com#1].

Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister after an inconclusive October 27 election. His rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has the first opportunity to form a government, while coalition discussions remain unsettled [ft.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1]. The Knesset, Israel’s parliament, also gave preliminary approval to a bill barring indicted lawmakers from forming a government; it must pass a committee stage and three further votes to become law [al-monitor.com#1]. Eisenkot’s mandate to form a government expires December 6, with a possible two-week extension [nzherald.co.nz#1].
quote: Today, the trial fell apart.
talking_points: Trial status: Netanyahu completed his testimony on June 24, and his defense team has since called witnesses [al-monitor.com#1].
Coalition shift: Eisenkot announced an agreement with Yisrael Beiteinu, led by Avigdor Lieberman, bringing his bloc closer to forming a government [nzherald.co.nz#1].
Alleged benefits: Bezeq’s former chairman Shaul Elovitch denied wrongdoing; prosecutors put the alleged regulatory benefits at about 1.8 billion shekels [japantoday.com#1].

perspectives.text: Gali Baharav-Miara, Israeli attorney general: She said prosecutors had already offered a plea agreement that Netanyahu’s side had not accepted, and that the case should conclude through a verdict or an appropriate agreement [middleeastmonitor.com#1].

Raz Nizri, former Israeli deputy attorney general: He argued that prosecutors had fallen into “groupthink,” urged an internal review and said the case did not prove the legal system was corrupt or Netanyahu had been politically framed [timesofisrael.com#2].
The Democrats party: The party halted coalition discussions with Eisenkot, saying the unity-government option with Likud and ultra-Orthodox parties should be taken off the table [nzherald.co.nz#1].

title: Spain’s snap election pits Sánchez against conservatives as Vox seeks kingmaker role
summary:
Nearly 39 million Spaniards are set to vote on Nov. 29 in an early general election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s eight years in office and bring the far-right Vox party into national government for the first time since Spain’s return to democracy [bbc.co.uk#1][politico.eu#1][touteleurope.eu#1]. Voters will elect the 350-member Congress and part of the Senate; parliament chooses the prime minister [politico.eu#1].

The conservative People’s Party (PP), led by Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leads most polls, followed closely by Sánchez’s Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE), with Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, in third place. Poll averages put the PP at about 31.5%, the Socialists at 29% and Vox at 17.9%; projections suggest the PP may need Vox’s support to reach a majority [rt-english.com#1][foreignpolicy.com#1][ynetnews.com#1].

Sánchez called the election after parliament rejected two housing measures on Oct. 2. His minority government has faced pressure over housing costs, living expenses, immigration and corruption investigations involving people close to him; the Bank of Spain estimates a shortage of about 700,000 homes [bbc.co.uk#1][bbc.co.uk#2][csmonitor.com#1]. After the vote count, parties must negotiate to form a government. A candidate for prime minister needs 176 votes in the first investiture ballot or more votes for than against in a second [politico.eu#1].
quote: Increases in employment or improved wages seem to count for little in public perception of the economy when inflation overwhelms everything else
quote_author: Juan Francisco Caro, director at social research institute Opina360
talking_points: Cost pressures: Spain’s inflation rate reached 4.9% in October, while average real wages fell 0.3% between 2019 and 2025; consumer confidence has dropped from 107 when Sánchez took office to 84.1 in the latest cited survey [straitstimes.com#1].

Youth discontent: Vox leads among voters under 35 in recent surveys, while just over one-third of households headed by someone under 35 owned a home in 2024, down from nearly 70% in 2011 [csmonitor.com#1].

Migration debate: Foreign nationals accounted for 3.7 million Social Security contributors in October, 16.4% of the total workforce, with substantial shares in hospitality, agriculture, construction and domestic work [bbc.com#1].

Seat mechanics: Spain allocates Congress seats across 50 provinces and Ceuta and Melilla using closed party lists and the D’Hondt method; smaller parties generally need more than the formal 3% threshold to win seats in low-seat districts [politico.eu#1][touteleurope.eu#1].

Foreign policy: The PP favors stronger ties with Washington and higher defense investment, while Sánchez has resisted U.S. use of Spanish bases for offensive operations against Iran [rt-english.com#1].

perspectives.text: Pedro Sánchez and the PSOE: Sánchez has made housing reform central to his campaign, calling for more homes—especially social housing—and regulation; he has also framed the choice as whether Spain should remain open and socially progressive or move toward the far right [touteleurope.eu#1][politico.eu#1].
People’s Party: Feijóo’s party advocates building more homes, tax relief for homebuyers and looser planning rules, and says it wants more controlled immigration [bbc.co.uk#1].

Vox: Vox calls for Spanish citizens to receive priority in access to benefits and public services, and advocates deportations of unauthorized migrants; it has also promoted a broader “remigration” policy [bbc.co.uk#1][csmonitor.com#1].
Young Vox supporters: Some young attendees said the party’s appeals to Spanish identity, unity and security resonated amid uncertainty and polarization [csmonitor.com#1].

Spanish small-business owners: One owner in Extremadura said she was likely to vote PP after a regional PP-Vox government cut taxes for small businesses; another said she wanted change despite differences with Vox [straitstimes.com#1].

title: Kim calls for wider tactical nuclear deployment as North Korea expands production
summary:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for deploying tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains and said the country was systematically expanding nuclear-material production, state media reported Thursday. He spoke during a Wednesday inspection of nuclear-material production and weapons research sites, including a newly built production base and a nuclear-related equipment facility. State media did not identify their locations [yna.co.kr#2][koreaherald.com#1][cnbc.com#1].

Kim said tactical weapons should serve different missions, citing what he described as threats from South Korea and the United States. He again declared North Korea’s nuclear status irreversible and warned that attempts to deny it would be treated as a declaration of war. Pyongyang enshrined its nuclear status in its constitution in 2023 [aljazeera.com#1][yna.co.kr#2].

The inspection followed President Donald Trump’s unsuccessful bid to meet Kim during a visit to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit last week. North Korea did not publicly respond; Trump later said the timing had not been right. South Korea’s defense ministry expressed grave concern over Kim’s stated intention to expand tactical weapons [euronews.com#1][thehindu.com#1][yna.co.kr#2].
quote: Our possession of nuclear weapons is an absolutely irreversible choice as long as malicious forces exist that use nuclear weapons as a means of achieving hegemony
quote_author: Kim Jong Un, North Korean leader
talking_points: Facility clues: Images released by North Korean state media showed equipment analysts identified as uranium-enrichment centrifuges and several apparent warhead designs. Analysts said the pictured equipment could be intended for a naval reactor program [japantoday.com#1][aawsat.com#1].

Production estimate: Weapons experts cited by NDTV estimated that North Korea’s annual fissile-material output has risen from about six bombs’ worth during Trump’s first term to roughly 12–15 bombs’ worth [ndtv.com#1].

Watchdog concern: International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi said North Korea had expanded its original uranium-enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling the development a serious concern [euronews.com#1][thehindu.com#1].
Monitoring limits: The IAEA has lacked access to North Korea since 2009 and monitors its activities using satellite imagery and open-source intelligence [cnbc.com#1].
Possible reach: South Korean analyst Shin Jong-woo said Kim’s reference to “multiple domains” could signal targets beyond the Korean Peninsula, including the U.S. mainland [dailymaverick.co.za#1].

perspectives.text: North Korean leadership: Kim framed the buildup as a response to alleged nuclear threats from the United States and its allies, and said Pyongyang would not seek other countries’ approval for its nuclear status [dw.com#1].

South Korean Defense Ministry: The ministry called on Pyongyang to stop justifying its nuclear program and comply with United Nations Security Council resolutions; it said Seoul would bolster deterrence with Washington [yna.co.kr#2].

Lim Eul-chul, Kyungnam University professor: Lim said the visit did not necessarily shut the door to U.S. dialogue, but signaled that North Korea would seek talks between states treated as nuclear powers [dailymaverick.co.za#1].

President Donald Trump: Trump said Kim had not ignored his meeting overture, described the summit schedule as too busy, and said contact could resume, though the two had not corresponded recently [thehindu.com#1].

title: B.C. premier orders bridge study, SOGI removal and office return
summary:
British Columbia Premier Lorne Doerkson on Wednesday ordered a design process for a bridge to replace the George Massey Tunnel, the removal of SOGI 123 school materials on sexual orientation and gender identity, and a phased return to the office for provincial employees. The orders follow mandate letters calling for the reversal of several policies of the previous NDP government [cbc.ca#1][cheknews.ca#2][theglobeandmail.com#1]. The notice of intent asks the tunnel’s current contractor to develop the bridge option. Doerkson said cabinet would review the costs before deciding and that he hoped to make a final choice before Christmas [cbc.ca#1].

Doerkson said SOGI 123 resources would be removed from government websites immediately, with school districts asked to remove them from schools [cbc.ca#1][cheknews.ca#2]. He also directed ministries to plan a phased return to the office, saying employees able to work from government offices would return five days a week [cbc.ca#1]. Other mandate-letter priorities include publicly funded treatment through another provider when waits exceed medically recommended limits, and an independent review of provincial finances [theglobeandmail.com#1][thetyee.ca#1].
quote: Our responsibility is to ensure taxpayers get the best value for their money.
talking_points: Health changes: The health minister was also directed to conduct a 100-day system review, recruit doctors and nurses, and keep rural emergency departments and maternity wards open [cheknews.ca#2].

Energy targets: The new environment minister is directed to repeal CleanBC and electric-vehicle sales targets, while the energy minister is directed to triple natural-gas production by 2035 [nationalobserver.com#1][cheknews.ca#2].

Mining permits: The mandate calls for fixed approval timelines for mines and exploration permits; Association for Mineral Exploration CEO Todd Stone said the sector welcomed the push to speed up permitting [vancouversun.com#4].

perspectives.text: BC Government Employees Union (BCGEU): President Paul Finch said the union was disappointed it was not consulted, urged the government to compare productivity under remote and office work, and argued that added office costs should be considered before implementation.

B.C. NDP interim leader Jennifer Whiteside: Whiteside said the mandate letters lacked clarity and warned that British Columbians would not want the previous government’s work on housing, health care, affordability and climate resilience undone.

Thomas Green, David Suzuki Foundation: Green argued that expanding gas production while cutting climate measures would benefit a small number of mostly foreign companies, and said eliminating industrial carbon pricing could expose B.C. gas to higher costs in European markets.

Association for Mineral Exploration, B.C.: CEO Todd Stone said the sector wants a framework to measure permitting progress, adding that the industry had made only modest progress under the previous government.

title: Carney says Trump has not raised Pentagon's Canada defence complaints
summary:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said U.S. President Donald Trump has not raised the Pentagon’s criticism of Canada’s defence spending in their conversations, as Ottawa and Washington dispute Canada’s military readiness and procurement plans [thestar.com#1][cbc.ca#1]. In a fact sheet released Monday, the Pentagon said Canada lacked a credible, fully costed plan to meet NATO’s spending goal and was limiting its contribution to North American defence [military.com#1][cbc.ca#1].

Carney said Canada is taking responsibility for its defence, citing its NATO deployment in Latvia and work with allies in the Arctic and Europe [theglobeandmail.com#1][cbc.ca#1]. Stephen Fuhr, secretary of state for defence procurement, acknowledged readiness shortfalls but said purchases and recruitment were accelerating [cbc.ca#1][thestar.com#1]. Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said the U.S. defence secretary should not dictate Canadian policy, while arguing that government spending has not adequately reached military personnel [cbc.ca#1]. NATO members are due to review their spending commitment in 2029 [military.com#1].
quote: He has not raised issues such as has been reported recently
talking_points: Budget targets: Canada’s latest budget projects combined defence and security spending of 4.1% of GDP in 2027-28, including 2.6% for core defence [military.com#1][eurasiantimes.com#1].

Cooperation limits: A Pentagon directive restricts some military engagement with Canadians at think-tank events and social functions; a senior U.S. official said it does not affect military operations [thestar.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1].

Fighter review: Canada has committed to 16 F-35s, while the rest of its planned 88-aircraft purchase remains under review; the Pentagon says a mixed fleet could put additional pressure on personnel and NORAD [theglobeandmail.com#1][newsday.com#1].

Procurement choices: Fuhr cited U.S.-made P-8 surveillance aircraft and HIMARS launchers as equipment Canada continues to buy, alongside Ottawa’s effort to buy more at home and from other partners [cbc.ca#1].

perspectives.text: U.S. Department of Defense: A senior department official said the engagement restrictions aim to ensure a unified objective in dealings with Canada and argued that Ottawa needs a realistic approach focused on military efficiency [theglobeandmail.com#1].

Stephen Fuhr, Secretary of State for Defence Procurement: Fuhr said U.S. officials may not have up-to-date information about the pace of Canadian changes and defended a strategy of diversifying procurement while continuing to buy American equipment [thestar.com#1][cbc.ca#1].

Stephen Saideman, Carleton University defence expert: Saideman said U.S. Defence Secretary Hegseth was trying to bully Canada into abandoning its plan to diversify defence spending and reduce reliance on U.S. suppliers [cbc.ca#1].

title: B.C. coastal communities face flood risk as king tides meet storms
summary:
British Columbia’s coast faced heightened flood risk as king tides coincided with heavy rain, strong winds and storm surge, prompting evacuation alerts, local states of emergency and ferry cancellations [cbc.ca#1][thestar.com#1]. Environment and Climate Change Canada warned that water levels in parts of Metro Vancouver could rise 40 to 70 centimetres above the year’s highest astronomical tides; levels along Vancouver Island and the central coast were forecast to rise 30 to 50 centimetres above those tides [cbc.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1]. The same high-tide episode brought flooding and destructive surf to California, while B.C.’s immediate threat came from tides combined with a series of storms [theglobeandmail.com#1].

Alerts covered low-lying communities on Vancouver Island, including Lantzville, Cedar and French Creek. Ahousaht declared a local state of emergency as water eroded its shoreline. Squamish also declared an emergency, as did the Comox Valley Regional District on Wednesday evening in response to rising water and flood risk [cbc.ca#1][thestar.com#1].

The B.C. River Forecast Centre upgraded a flood watch between Nanaimo and Campbell River, and Environment Canada warned that warm temperatures could bring rain on snow, increasing runoff. Authorities also warned of coastal erosion and urged residents to move valuables and toxic chemicals out of basements. Forecasters expected the highest tides Thursday [cbc.ca#1][thestar.com#1].
quote: As part of the state of emergency, we are taking proactive measures and doing sandbagging... and doing impromptu or proactive diking
talking_points: Rainfall totals: A Vancouver Island monitoring station recorded 469 millimetres of rain between 11 a.m. Monday and 1 p.m. Wednesday, while winds reached nearly 160 km/h off the island’s northern tip [theglobeandmail.com#1][thestar.com#1]
Road disruption: Highway 16 on Haida Gwaii closed Tuesday after debris and water covered the road [cbc.ca#1]
Local preparation: Delta said it was preparing low-lying coastal neighbourhoods, while Tofino and Ucluelet closed public beach access ahead of the storms [cbc.ca#1]
Residents at risk: Squamish officials said they were paying particular attention to an encampment along waterways, where unhoused residents faced direct exposure to flooding [cbc.ca#1]

perspectives.text: Quadra Island resident Marc Doll said a smaller bridge on his property was swept away, leaving 12 pigs cut off. He waded through thigh-deep water to feed a sow and her eight piglets [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Kyuquot resident Nicalena Chidley said the storm had already caused significant damage to her dock [ctvnews.ca#1].

title: Ontario liquor retailer adds police at 40-plus stores to deter theft
summary:
The Liquor Control Board of Ontario (LCBO), the province’s liquor retailer, will deploy paid-duty police officers at more than 40 stores under a new campaign called Operation Secure Stores. The officers will work with local police in Toronto, Durham, Peel and York regions, while the LCBO adds guards and covert security personnel at stores it identifies as high-risk [globalnews.ca#1][cbc.ca#1][nowtoronto.com#1].

The LCBO says organized crime groups account for about 70 per cent of its theft-related losses and that existing security measures led to more than 2,000 arrests in the past year [sootoday.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1]. The operation will focus on repeat offenders and improve information-sharing with police; third-party guards will receive refresher training on preventing theft, handling tense situations and gathering evidence [nowtoronto.com#1][cbc.ca#1].
quote: It's a recognition of the extent of organized retail crime and at the same time, the limitations of private security guards.
quote_author: Ian Messenger, professor of public safety at Seneca Polytechnic
talking_points: Store network: The LCBO operates more than 690 stores carrying high-value goods, according to Global News [globalnews.ca#1].
Guard authority: The LCBO says its plainclothes security personnel can intervene in thefts and make arrests on site [cbc.ca#1].
Seasonal rationale: The LCBO said the security push is intended to protect customers, staff and products as the holiday season approaches [cbc.ca#1].

Earlier probe: Months earlier, Toronto police released the results of a widespread retail-theft investigation that led to hundreds of arrests. Video shown at the news conference showed masked people entering a Toronto LCBO, filling bags and suitcases, and leaving with them [cp24.com#1].

perspectives.text: LCBO: Senior Director of Resource Protection Al Almeida said the campaign uses data analysis to direct security resources to stores where they are most needed [nowtoronto.com#1].

Toronto Police Service: Deputy Chief Lauren Pogue said Toronto Police supports the initiative and its shared commitment to safer environments for employees, customers and communities [nowtoronto.com#1].

title: Montreal police charge third former officer in racism investigation
summary:
Montreal police arrested and charged former officer Youcef Boumsied, 33, with assault over an alleged incident on or around Aug. 31, 2024. He is the third recently fired officer charged in the investigation into alleged racism and misconduct at Station 39 in Montréal-Nord [cbc.ca#1][radio-canada.ca#1][globalnews.ca#1]. Boumsied was released on a promise to appear; no court date has been set. Two other former officers, Zachary Belzil and Vincent Routhier, face assault and breach-of-trust charges. Belzil also faces a criminal-harassment charge. Both are due in court Dec. 8 [theglobeandmail.com#1][thestar.com#1].

The charges follow the firing of seven officers from two Montreal stations as criminal investigations continue. Allegations tied to Station 39 include officers cutting racialized civilians’ hair and keeping it as trophies. None of the allegations against the charged officers has been tested in court [cbc.ca#1][globalnews.ca#1]. Quebec’s prosecution service said it would not comment further on the latest case, while Montreal police said related investigations remain underway [cbc.ca#1].
quote: In the end, we judge a police officer by the way they treat those who cannot defend themselves.
talking_points: Internal reporting: The police chief said he was encouraged that Station 39 officers reported colleagues, saying it showed they felt able to break the “code of silence” [ledevoir.com#1].
Other allegations: Separate allegations involving Station 21 include an officer humiliating people experiencing homelessness, including by allegedly urinating on them [cbc.ca#1][globalnews.ca#1].
Independent oversight: An independent observer appointed by Quebec’s Ministry of Internal Security is overseeing the criminal investigations [cbc.ca#1][journaldemontreal.com#1].
Public disclosure: Quebec’s prosecution service said it announced the third charge publicly to preserve public confidence in the justice system [ledevoir.com#1].

perspectives.text: Montreal police: The force said discriminatory or racist behaviour is unacceptable and will not be tolerated [cbc.ca#1].
Montreal police brotherhood: The union is contesting the seven dismissals, arguing the process was arbitrary and did not respect principles of natural justice [radio-canada.ca#1].

Fo Niemi, Center for Research-Action on Race Relations executive director: Niemi called for a systemic review of officer recruitment, training and supervision, and said authorities should clarify what support alleged victims are receiving [citynews.ca#1].

title: European Space Agency's Hera probe reveals stadium-sized crater from NASA asteroid test
summary:
The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has revealed that NASA’s 2022 impact test carved a crater spanning nearly the full width of Dimorphos, a 151-meter asteroid moonlet, and left it tumbling chaotically around its larger companion, Didymos. Hera’s first close-up images also show hundreds of boulders around the pair; neither asteroid poses a threat to Earth [esa.int#1][science.org#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) shortened Dimorphos’s orbital period around Didymos by 33 minutes, but scientists had not seen the collision’s physical effects in detail. Hera’s measurements are intended to show how the asteroid’s shape, mass and structure affected the deflection and help refine predictions for future impact missions [esa.int#1][theguardian.com#1][thehindu.com#1].

Hera is surveying the asteroids from about 25 to 30 kilometers away. The European Space Agency (ESA) plans to move Hera closer in December 2026 and deploy two CubeSats in January 2027; one is designed to use radar to examine Dimorphos’s interior [esa.int#1][popsci.com#1][theregister.com#1].
quote: Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once!
talking_points: Uneven damage: Hera’s images show little apparent change to the boulder fields on the side of Dimorphos opposite the impact, despite the crater across the struck face [esa.int#1][dawn.com#1].

Boulder hazard: The newly observed rocks range from tens of centimeters to several meters, and their origin—impact debris or material already in the system—has not been established [nzz.ch#1][krdo.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].
Image resolution: Hera's first close-up imagery resolved features at about 2.7 meters per pixel [astronomynow.com#1][vietnamplus.vn#1].
DART benchmark: NASA had defined a reduction of at least 73 seconds in Dimorphos’s orbital period as a successful test; the measured change was about 33 minutes [sciencealert.com#1][space.com#1].
Surface composition: Italy’s Milani CubeSat is tasked with examining the asteroid’s surface composition and surrounding dust [esa.int#1][engadget.com#1][theregister.com#1].

perspectives.text: Ian Whittaker, a physics lecturer at Nottingham Trent University, cautioned that predicting a deflection is not straightforward because the result depends partly on how much material an asteroid ejects when struck [theguardian.com#1].

timeline.content: NASA’s DART spacecraft deliberately struck Dimorphos in a deflection test [esa.int#1][science.org#1].
ESA launched Hera to study the aftermath of the DART collision [space.com#2][theguardian.com#1].
Hera reached the Didymos system after its two-year journey [elpais.com#1].
Hera photographed the asteroid pair from about 29 kilometers away [astronomynow.com#1].
ESA released Hera’s first close-up images of the impact site [esa.int#1][science.org#1].
Hera is scheduled to approach to roughly 13 kilometers from the asteroids [esa.int#1][popsci.com#1].
Hera plans to deploy two CubeSats for closer asteroid studies [esa.int#1][theregister.com#1].

did_you_know: Didymos’s surface gravity is about 40,000 times weaker than Earth’s, according to Hera team member Naomi Murdoch [bbc.co.uk#1].

technical_details: Momentum transfer: Measuring Dimorphos’s mass alongside its observed orbital change will help researchers estimate how efficiently DART transferred momentum, including the contribution of ejected material [theregister.com#1][theguardian.com#1].

Hera instruments: The spacecraft’s Asteroid Framing Camera records monochrome images, Hyperscout H observes in 25 spectral bands, and JAXA’s Thermal Infrared Imager measures surface temperature [esa.int#1][eldiario.es#1].

Close-range radar: The Juventas CubeSat is designed to use low-frequency radar to probe the asteroid’s interior, a measurement that could constrain its internal structure [esa.int#1][theregister.com#1].
scientific_significance: Impact physics: DART’s mass, speed and trajectory were known, and Hera’s images can be compared with pre-impact views, giving researchers an unusual dataset for studying impacts at asteroid scale [theguardian.com#1].

Rubble-pile behavior: Dimorphos is thought to be an aggregate of smaller rocks held together by extremely weak gravity, making its response to an impact harder to predict than that of a solid body [sciencealert.com#1].
System-wide effects: DART changed not only Dimorphos’s orbit around Didymos but also the binary pair’s orbit around the Sun [scientificamerican.com#1].
historical_background: The collision destroyed DART, and impact debris obscured the site from the accompanying LICIACube spacecraft. By the time the dust cleared, LICIACube had departed, leaving Hera to document the crater directly [sciencealert.com#1][theregister.com#1].

title: Army says Iowa blast produced no detectable airborne lead; testing continues
summary:
The U.S. Army says air monitors detected no airborne lead after it detonated the nation’s stockpile of degraded lead azide Wednesday at its Iowa ammunition plant. Officials later lifted the shelter-in-place order for nearby residents [bbc.co.uk#1][nebraskaexaminer.com#1][newsday.com#2]. The blast destroyed 68 barrels of the explosive, which the Army said had become unstable in storage and could detonate without warning [pbs.org#1][theguardian.com#1].

The initial air readings are not the final environmental assessment. The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services said it would review soil-sampling results before deciding whether further public-health advice is needed. The Army and Federal Emergency Management Agency said more testing and updates would follow [nebraskaexaminer.com#1][newsday.com#2].

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said it had collected more than 1,200 air, land and water samples before the blast and would continue monitoring. NASA deployed research aircraft and used its space-based TEMPO pollution instrument to collect environmental and atmospheric data, while independent researchers planned further testing. Laboratory analysis of environmental samples is expected to take days to weeks, Purdue University environmental engineering professor Andrew Whelton said [nebraskaexaminer.com#1][cbs2iowa.com#1][newsday.com#2].
quote: The lead-up to the detonation should never have been so chaotic and unclear
talking_points: NASA monitoring: NASA deployed a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III and a B200 research aircraft, and used its space-based TEMPO pollution instrument to observe the event [cbs2iowa.com#1][space.com#1].
Follow-up guidance: Whelton said eventual recommendations could differ among communities based on distance from the detonation area and whether they were upwind or downwind [newsday.com#2].

perspectives.text: U.S. Army: Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley called the operation successful and said mitigation measures reduced the risk to nearby residents to as close to zero as possible [nebraskaexaminer.com#1].

Rob Sand, Iowa governor-elect: Sand called for immediate transparency about how the crisis developed and said officials should continue testing before expressing certainty about its effects [theguardian.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

Iowa environmental groups: The groups argued that lead settling on land or entering waterways could expose people, livestock and wildlife even after airborne dust dissipates [newsday.com#1][ndtv.com#1].

A federal appeals court ruling put the detonation back on track, and the Army set the blast for Wednesday [pbs.org#1][koaa.com#1]

title: Pakistan's Zeeshan Ali becomes first foreign astronaut aboard China's Tiangong station
summary:
Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has entered China’s Tiangong space station, becoming the first foreign astronaut to visit the outpost and the first Pakistani to reach orbit. Shenzhou-24 docked on Nov. 25 after launching from Jiuquan, China, carrying Ali, Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The flight is the first joint mission with a foreign astronaut in China’s crewed space program [afp.com#1][apnews.com#1][thecitizen.co.tz#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

Ali is assigned four China-Pakistan research projects in biotechnology and materials, including tests involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria, quinoa seeds and composite materials. The mission includes more than 90 experiments and technology tests in fields including life sciences, materials science, physics and space medicine [ichongqing.info#1][nation.com.pk#1][brecorder.com#2].

Ali is expected to spend five days to a week aboard Tiangong, then return to Earth with two members of the Shenzhou-23 crew aboard their spacecraft. Chinese astronauts Tang and Wu are scheduled to remain for the usual six-month rotation, while Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu will stay for a year as researchers study how prolonged spaceflight affects the human body [theguardian.com#1][brecorder.com#1][faz.net#1].
quote: What comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself
quote_author: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Pakistani astronaut and payload specialist
talking_points: Research range: Fundamental-physics work will use optical-lattice quantum simulation to explore new states of matter and test a space cold-atom interferometer for inertial measurement [ichongqing.info#1].
Crew milestone: Tang Hongbo is set to become the first astronaut to visit Tiangong three times [ichongqing.info#1].

Training demands: Ali trained in Beijing for seven months, including intensive Chinese-language instruction because spacecraft controls, software and voice announcements operate in Chinese [theguardian.com#1][ft.com#1].
Station capacity: Tiangong can host up to six astronauts during crew handovers, allowing Shenzhou-24’s arrival to overlap with the departing crew [thecitizen.co.tz#1].

perspectives.text: Blaine Curcio, space industry consultant: Curcio said sending another country’s astronaut requires substantial trust and gives Pakistan detailed insight into China’s crewed space program. He said the mission could show other countries that Beijing is open to similar cooperation [theguardian.com#1].

Ahsan Iqbal, Pakistan's planning minister: Iqbal said the flight could lead to expanded cooperation, including a possible joint lunar mission. He said it shows how developing countries can build capabilities in strategically important areas [thecitizen.co.tz#1].

title: Judge blocks FCC’s early review of eight Disney-owned ABC station licenses
summary:
A federal judge on Wednesday barred the Federal Communications Commission from continuing its early review of eight broadcast licenses held by Disney-owned ABC, ruling that the network is likely to show the FCC retaliated against it for speech critical of President Trump [npr.org#1][latimes.com#1]. The preliminary injunction pauses the review while ABC and Disney’s lawsuit proceeds; U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan also rejected the FCC’s bid to dismiss the case [cnbc.com#1][politico.com#1].

The FCC ordered the stations to seek early renewals in April, although their licenses were not due for renewal until 2028 at the earliest. The agency said its action related to an investigation of Disney’s diversity and employment practices. AliKhan found that the timing, public statements by Trump and FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, and the potential loss of licenses supported ABC’s retaliation claim [latimes.com#1][reason.com#1][cbsnews.com#1].

AliKhan did not bar the FCC from taking other future actions against ABC, saying she could not issue a blanket injunction against unspecified threats [latimes.com#1][cbsnews.com#1]. The FCC said it disagreed with the decision and expects to prevail; the lawsuit will continue [politico.com#1][dw.com#1].
quote: Chairman Carr has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders
talking_points: Business exposure: ABC’s owned stations serve six of the 10 largest U.S. markets, including New York, Los Angeles and Houston, and contribute significantly to the network’s bottom line [npr.org#1].

Editorial changes: ABC said pressure had affected its editorial choices: “The View” stopped inviting political candidates ahead of the 2026 elections, and a Senate candidate’s “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” interview appeared on YouTube rather than broadcast television [npr.org#1][cnbc.com#1].

FCC rationale: The commission said it accelerated the review because it was investigating whether Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion practices violated anti-discrimination rules. It said Disney had not adequately answered its information requests [npr.org#1][cbsnews.com#1].

Narrow injunction: AliKhan barred further steps in the early license-renewal proceedings but denied ABC’s request to prohibit any other formal or informal FCC actions aimed at influencing editorial discretion [latimes.com#1][deadline.com#1].

FCC response: The FCC called the ruling wrong on the facts and the law and said it would continue using its authority to enforce broadcasters’ public-interest obligations [politico.com#1][channel3000.com#1].

perspectives.text: Federal Communications Commission: The agency maintains that the review arose from its investigation into Disney’s diversity and employment practices, not ABC’s programming, and says broadcasters must meet public-interest obligations [cbsnews.com#1][politico.com#1].

ABC and Disney: The companies argued the early review itself caused irreparable First Amendment harm by forcing broadcasters to weigh independent editorial decisions against the risk of losing valuable licenses [cbsnews.com#1].

Anna M. Gomez, FCC commissioner: The commission’s sole Democratic member said the ruling should prompt broadcasters facing pressure to defend their rights rather than capitulate [npr.org#1][thehill.com#1].

Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press: President Bruce Brown called the decision a win for all broadcasters, arguing that the case was novel because of the administration’s punitive actions [deadline.com#1].
